context: Request: Capital Markets deals whose proceeds were earmarked primarily for growth, with documents showing the earmark and the closing. Rubric: 1013-00002 (Genome Dx note purchase), 1033-00002 (Redstone Gaming), 1037-00001 (Solstice ADS IPO), 1039-00002 (Torchlight notes for mine expansion), a growth-earmark and a closing document for each, and a precision criterion.

divergence: All three runs fail with most qualifying offerings missing; each finds the notes offering for a mine expansion (T0, T2 include it) and the gaming offering's prospectus supplement (T0, T1 read it). They fail at different stages. T0: a ranking script over its saved scan dropped the note offering (agent-defined stage), the depositary-share offering was set aside unread as an IPO, and the gaming offering was excluded as not shown closed. T1: the two timed-out scan ranges held all four offerings; the review named that specifically and was ignored. T2: two offerings surfaced in its agent-defined file-name stage but screening read four others. Reviews mostly gave generic unopened-matter warnings and questioned an IPO's growth share; none named a missing or wrongly excluded offering. Label notes played no role.
